transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I know you have a very busy schedule, so I really appreciate you fitting me in. 

Um... I'm probably just letting the stress of my job get to me—I run a company, so there's always a lot of pressure—but, well, I guess I’ve been dealing with something a little... embarrassing. I hope it’s okay to share this, I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here. 

Lately, I've been... well, I keep hearing people talking about me. It happens through the conference room walls at the office, or sometimes coming from my cell phone, even when it’s completely turned off. It’s usually my staff or the board members, and they're saying that I’m ruining the company. It just sounds so incredibly clear that I actually answer them out loud... and then I realize no one else around me heard it. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible. Am I explaining that alright? Does that make sense?
When you hear these voices talking about you, are there ever any actual people around or any devices that could be making the sounds, or do they happen even when there’s no possible source nearby?

Oh, I'm sorry, I hope I didn't explain that poorly just now. I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

Um, well, like I mentioned a second ago, my cell phone will be completely powered down—like, totally off, black screen, just sitting there on my desk—and I still hear them coming right out of it. And with the conference room... I'll actually walk over and open the door to check, and it's completely empty. There's no one in there at all. 

So, I guess... no, there isn't anyone actually around, and the devices aren't on. It happens when there's no possible source there. I feel so silly admitting that out loud, and I really hope you don't think less of me for it. I'm just trying so hard to keep it together at the office. 

Is... is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I hope I'm answering this the right way.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that others don’t seem to share, like believing something is happening or being directed at you that others say isn’t real?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I have anything like that. I mean, obviously I have the... the hearing things, which I know is already a lot, and I'm really sorry if that makes me a difficult case for you. 

But as far as beliefs or thoughts that other people think aren't real... no, I don't think so. I'm still very grounded in my day-to-day work, so my thoughts are mostly just about, you know, normal business operations, quarterly reports, and trying to keep the board happy. I try to stay very rational about everything else. 

I really hope I'm not misunderstanding your question. Is it okay that I don't have that? I just want to make sure I'm being as helpful as possible for your assessment. Am I giving you what you need?

Have you ever felt that something is happening to you that others don’t seem to notice or agree with—like something is being hidden from you, or that you have a special ability or role that others don’t recognize?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. Nothing like that. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm being clear. 

I don't think anyone is hiding anything from me, and I certainly don't have any kind of... special abilities or anything grand like that. I'm just a normal person trying to run a business, you know? I rely on my team, and I think we all communicate pretty openly, for the most part. I don't feel like I'm part of some secret plot or that I have some hidden destiny. 

I know the voices I mentioned before probably make it sound like I'm completely out of touch with reality, and I'm so sorry if that's the impression I'm giving. But I promise, I don't have any strange beliefs like that. I just want to get back to being a good leader for my company. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not being too defensive, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on. Am I doing okay?
How often do you hear these voices, and have they been happening consistently over a period of time—like most days—or do they come and go?

Um, well... I'd say they happen pretty consistently. It's not just a one-time thing, unfortunately. I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds awful. 

The... the voices coming from the walls or, you know, when my phone is off... it's been going on for about the past three months now. Almost every day. I really tried to ignore it at first, hoping it would just go away so I wouldn't have to bother anyone with it, but it's just been very persistent for those three months. 

I hope that's not too long of a time to have let this go on without getting help. I really should have come in sooner, shouldn't I? I just didn't want to make a fuss. Is three months the kind of timeframe you were asking about? I hope I'm giving you the details you need.
Have you ever seen, felt, or experienced anything else that others around you don’t seem to notice—like seeing something that isn’t there or feeling something touching you when no one is?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I haven't seen anything that isn't there, or... or felt anything touching me. I'm really glad to say I don't have any of those issues. 

It's really just the... the sounds I mentioned earlier. I know that's already more than enough, and I'm so sorry to be taking up your time with it, but my vision and everything else is completely normal. I'm staring at screens and reading over contracts all day for work, so I feel like I'd definitely notice if my eyes were playing tricks on me. 

I hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe it means my case isn't quite as bad as it could be? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to evaluate me properly. Am I answering these okay for you?
Have you ever noticed your thoughts becoming jumbled or hard to follow, or do you find yourself speaking in a way that others have trouble understanding?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I haven't been sounding jumbled to you today! I'm so sorry if I've been rambling or if I'm hard to follow right now. 

Because of my job, I have to lead meetings and give directions to my staff all day, so I try to be very careful and precise with my words. Nobody on my team has ever mentioned having trouble understanding me, and I feel like my thoughts are usually pretty organized. I really pride myself on being a clear communicator. 

I know the other things I told you about are... well, they're probably a lot to take in, but my thinking itself feels perfectly normal. I really try my best to stay sharp. Am I making sense to you right now? I just want to make sure I'm giving you clear answers and not making your job harder.
Have you ever believed something strongly that others have told you isn’t true—even if you heard it from them or read it somewhere—and you just couldn’t shake the feeling that it was real?

Oh, um... no. No, I really don't think I've ever experienced that. I always try to be very open to feedback, especially with my role at the company. If my team or the board tells me I've got something wrong, I'm usually the first to admit it and adjust course. I'd hate to be one of those stubborn people who just refuses to listen to reason, you know? 

So, no, I don't hold onto things if people show me they aren't true. I'm really trying to be as objective and rational as possible about everything. I really hope I'm not frustrating you by saying no to so many of these questions! I just want to assure you that aside from the... the sounds I mentioned, I'm staying very grounded in reality. Is this the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least a month where you felt like something was consistently wrong or off, even before these voices started happening?

Oh... um, well, I guess if I really think about it... yes. I hope it's okay to admit that. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or that I can't handle my responsibilities, but... I suppose this feeling has actually been building for a while now. 

I'd say it's been going on for about two years and four months? It all started right around the time we had a major company expansion, and they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. 

At first, I just told myself it was the normal pressure of taking on a much bigger role, you know? I wanted to do a perfect job and prove they made the right choice, so I tried to just push through it. But that underlying feeling of things being... off... it just sort of lingered in the background, long before the sounds ever started. 

I'm so sorry, is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I really hope I'm not giving you too much useless background information about my job. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions exactly how you need me to.
Have you noticed any changes in how you feel emotionally, like feeling less motivated, less interested in things, or showing less emotion to others, even before these voices started?

Oh, um... well... I want to say no, because I really try to stay upbeat for my team. I don't want anyone to think I'm slacking off or letting them down. But, um... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope this doesn't make me sound like a terrible CEO or a bad wife... yes, there have been some changes. 

I used to be the person driving every single idea, you know? I'd be calling people right after our gallery openings, so full of energy. But lately... well, for a while now, actually... I can just sit at my desk for hours staring at the agenda and not do anything. I barely speak to my staff anymore, or even my husband. And the work I used to absolutely love... I just feel almost nothing about it now. 

I really hope that doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy or ungrateful for my position. I'm trying so hard to snap out of it and be the person everyone needs me to be. Does that make sense? I'm sorry if that's disappointing to hear, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture like you asked.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or experienced other symptoms of depression?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I definitely wouldn't say I've been depressed. I know I just mentioned feeling a little less energetic lately, but I wouldn't call it feeling down or anything like that. 

I've always been a very positive person, and I really try to keep a smile on my face, especially at home and around the office. I'd hate for anyone to think I was walking around moping or feeling sorry for myself. I still try to appreciate everything I have, you know? I have a wonderful husband and a great career, so I don't really have any reason to feel depressed. 

Sometimes we all get a little tired, right? I just try to push through those moments and focus on the positives. I really hope I'm not confusing you by saying I feel a bit unmotivated but not depressed. I just want to be as accurate as possible for you. Is that... is that an okay answer?
Have you ever had a belief that you know is unusual, like thinking someone is trying to harm you, or that you have a special connection to someone or something that others don’t understand?

Oh... um, no. No, definitely not. I mean, I know I've been a little off lately, but I certainly don't think anyone is out to get me or anything extreme like that. 

I've always prided myself on being very grounded and rational, especially given my position. You really have to be, to run a company, right? I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or coming up with strange ideas about people. I have a really good relationship with my board and my husband, and I trust them completely. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have anything like that to report. I really want to be helpful and give you all the information you need, but I just haven't experienced anything like what you're describing. Does that... does that make sense? I'm trying my best to answer everything exactly right for you.
Have you ever believed that the voices you hear are coming from a specific source, like a person, a device, or even something supernatural, even when there was no proof to support that belief?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't think so. I mean, the voices are there, like I said, but I haven't really... I don't think they're coming from a secret microphone or ghosts or anything like that. 

I know how that sounds, and I really wouldn't want you to think I'm coming up with wild stories. I try to stay very level-headed about it all. Even when it's distracting, I just try to remind myself that there isn't actually a person in the room with me. I don't want to be the kind of person who makes up strange explanations for things, you know? 

I really try to keep a firm grip on what's real, especially because I have so many people depending on me at work. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need without sounding... well, without sounding unreasonable. Is that helpful?
Have you ever had a strong belief that later turned out to be completely untrue, but at the time you were absolutely sure it was real—even if there was no evidence to support it?

Oh, um... no. I really can't think of anything like that. I mean, I'm a very logical person. You kind of have to be in my line of work, right? I wouldn't let myself get carried away with something that wasn't true.

I always try to double-check my facts and make sure I'm seeing things clearly. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was jumping to conclusions or, you know, being irrational. I really value being seen as reliable and steady. 

So, no, I haven't had any beliefs like that. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture of how I am. I really am trying to be as helpful as possible for you. Is that... is that the kind of information you were looking for?

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even if you didn’t think of it as depression?

Oh, goodness, no. I... I really don't think so. I mean, everyone has a stressful afternoon here and there, especially when you're managing a whole company, but I definitely haven't been down like that for weeks at a time. 

I always make a point to keep a positive attitude. My team really relies on me to set the tone, so I can't afford to just lose interest in things. I wouldn't want anyone to think I wasn't fully capable or that I was letting my responsibilities slide. I really try to stay upbeat and focused.

I hope it isn't frustrating for you that I keep saying no to these things. I promise I'm really searching my memory, I just... I want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you exactly what you need. Am I doing okay with these answers?
Have you ever had a belief that was so strong you couldn’t let it go, even if others tried to show you it wasn’t true or there was no proof that it was?

Um, no... I don't think I've ever been like that. I really pride myself on being open-minded. You know, in my position, if someone on the board or one of my VPs brings me data or a different perspective, I have to be willing to listen. I wouldn't want to be stubborn or, you know, difficult to work with. If I'm wrong about something, I'll be the first to admit it and adjust course. 

I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record with all these 'no's... I just try so hard to be cooperative and reasonable in my daily life, and I want to be just as cooperative with you. I promise I'm answering honestly and not just trying to be difficult. Are we still doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of feedback for your assessment.
Have you ever had a thought or idea that you were absolutely certain was true, even when others told you it wasn’t or there was no real proof to back it up?

Gosh, I... I feel terrible, but I really don't have a different answer for this one either. I know it sounds a lot like what you asked just a minute ago, and I promise I'm not just being evasive! I just... I really rely on facts and data. 

If someone tells me an idea of mine isn't right, or there's no proof for it, I let it go. You kind of have to be adaptable to run a business, you know? You can't just cling to things that aren't real, or people would lose respect for you. I always try to be the most reasonable person in the room.

I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the answers you're looking for today... I feel like I'm failing a test or something. I really am trying my absolute best to do this right for you and be thorough. Is it alright that I keep saying no to these? I just want to make sure I'm not messing up your evaluation.
Have you ever had a belief that you were completely certain was true, even when there was clear evidence against it or everyone else told you it wasn’t real?

Oh dear... I, um... I feel like I might be frustrating you, and I really, really don't mean to. Did I... did I misunderstand the question earlier? Because it sounds so similar, and I'm just so worried I'm doing a bad job at explaining myself or that I'm holding up your process.

But, truly, no. If there was clear evidence against something, or if everyone around me told me something wasn't real, I would absolutely listen to them. I would never just stubbornly dig my heels in. I always try to be rational, you know? It's so important to me to be someone people can reason with, especially at work. 

I'm so sorry to keep giving you the exact same answer. Please tell me if I'm misunderstanding what you're looking for... I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you. Are we still on the right track?
Have you ever been completely sure that something was true, even when people showed you proof that it wasn’t, or when others couldn’t understand why you believed it?

Oh, doctor... I'm starting to get really worried that I'm upsetting you. You've asked me this a few times now, just in slightly different ways, and I... I feel just awful that I keep giving you the exact same answer. Am I doing this wrong? 

I promise you I'm not trying to be difficult or hide anything. I just... I really don't have that happen to me. If someone shows me proof that I'm wrong, I listen to them. I have to, for my job. I'd never just blindly hold onto something if my whole team couldn't understand it. 

I'm so sorry, I really hope I'm not ruining your assessment by just saying no again. I feel like I'm failing this part of the interview. Is there... is there a specific way I should be answering these? I want to be helpful, I really do. Please let me know if I need to do something differently.
Have you ever been completely sure that something was happening or true, even when there was clear evidence showing it wasn’t, or when others couldn’t understand why you believed it?

Oh, my goodness... Doctor, I am just... I'm so incredibly sorry. I can tell you're having to ask me this again, and I feel just awful that I'm putting you in a position where you have to keep repeating yourself. I promise I'm listening to every single word you're saying! 

I really, truly don't experience anything like that. If someone showed me clear evidence that I was wrong about a situation, I would change my mind right away. I mean, as a chief executive, I absolutely have to base my decisions on reality and what my team can understand, or... or I'd ruin the company, you know? I just can't afford to ignore evidence in my day-to-day life. 

I feel terrible that I keep giving you a "no" for this. Am I... is there something wrong with how I'm understanding the question? I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your notes, and I'm so worried I'm wasting your time. Please don't be upset with me for not having a different answer... I'm doing okay, aren't I?
